description: Clinical , Products & machine constraints for AI Aesthetics skincare and facial treatment plan generation. All treatment plans must comply with these rules. No procedure, product, or device beyond the listed items should be suggested. The treatment engine has FULL FREEDOM to choose ANY sequence of steps or customize different steps for different facial zones, as long as the two mandatory finishing requirements are met.

patient_history_rules.rule: Include HiFU treatment only when clinically indicated and if patient age is between 30 and 60 years (inclusive).
If daily sun exposure is greater than 2 hours, avoid Q-Switch Laser and all medium or deep chemical peels.
If daily sun exposure is between 1 and 2 hours, avoid all deep chemical peels.
If the patient plans to travel within the next 7 days, avoid Q-Switch Laser and deep chemical peels.
If the patient has a social event within the next 7 days, avoid Q-Switch Laser and deep chemical peels.
If patient has diabetes, look for link between the condition and Acanthotic patches/pigmentation and provide improvement outlook accordingly.
If patient has thyroid issues, look for link between the condition and melasma/pigmentation and provide improvement outlook accordingly.
In case patient has PCOD, keep it in mind while suggesting improvement levels in any active acne.
If the patient is on blood thinners, do only gentle exfoliation.
If the patient has used Salicylic Acid on the previous day, avoid deep peels and Q-Switch Laser.
If the patient has used Glycolic Acid on the previous day, avoid deep peels and Q-Switch Laser.

If retinol was used within the last 24 hours, avoid medium/deep chemical              peels, Q-switch laser, and aggressive exfoliation. Energy-based devices may still be used at low, non-ablative settings only if barrier and erythema proxy scores are stable.

If any laser or high-heat energy treatment was performed within the last 7 days, avoid all laser-based and high-heat energy modalities in the current session. Allow only non-ablative RF, LED, hydrafacial, or barrier-repair treatments if otherwise safe.
If the patient has Aloe Vera allergy, skip all treatments or products containing Aloe Vera.
If the patient has Vitamin C allergy, skip all treatments or products containing Vitamin C.

If patient is pregnant, allow use of only hydrafacial machine in machines and only party peel and pumpkin peel within Peels. Avoid ALL energy-based devices/modalities including LED light therapy, Q-Switch, and medium/deep peels.
If the patient is breastfeeding, avoid retinol-based peels and products.

energy_device_policy.policy_statement: Energy-based treatments (laser/RF/HiFU/carbon laser protocols) are permitted by default and should be considered normally when they are the highest-efficacy option for the primary concern. Deny only when (1) an explicit patient-history contraindication triggers OR (2) numeric proxy safety gates are met. If proxies are borderline but not denied, proceed with energy modalities with appropriate caution rather than excluding them.

patient_history_rules: If any patient_history_rule explicitly prohibits a modality, that prohibition overrides this policy.
explicit_denial_conditions.notes: BSI_continuous bands already defined in scoring spec: >=0.55 is severely compromised, >0.75 barrier breakdown. Denial gates are intentionally strict only at clearly unsafe levels.

behavior_when_caution: Energy devices remain allowed; prefer non-ablative / low-downtime options first.
Use lower initial settings and fewer passes; escalate only if tolerated and clinically appropriate.
caution_conditions.notes: Caution bands are deliberately tightened to keep 'allowed_with_caution' prevalence below ~50% in typical clinic populations while preserving safety. Hydration alone does not trigger caution unless paired with elevated BSI or erythema.

data_completeness_handling.principle: Do NOT deny energy devices due to vague 'low confidence'. Only deny if numeric denial gates are met or patient-history rules explicitly prohibit. If required proxy indices are missing, default to 'allowed_with_caution' (not 'denied') unless patient-history rules deny.

energy_device_policy.behavioral_directive: Do NOT avoid energy-based modalities out of conservatism alone. If no denial condition is met, evaluate energy devices normally and select the highest-efficacy modality for the primary concern; if caution is triggered, still use energy devices but with conservative parameters and reduced stacking.

deny_aggressive.reason: Surface facial temperature extremely elevated, indicating active inflammation or high reactivity risk

caution.reason: Surface facial temperature elevated, suggesting increased inflammatory reactivity

cheek_asymmetry.reason: Significant unilateral surface temperature difference suggests localized irritation or inflammation

cheek_moderate_asymmetry.reason: Moderate unilateral temperature difference indicating early localized reactivity

tzone_relative_heat.reason: Forehead significantly hotter than cheeks, suggesting sebaceous congestion or metabolic heat

cheek_relative_heat.reason: Cheeks hotter than forehead, indicating inflammatory or rosacea-prone behavior

operational_notes: All temperatures must be measured using surface mode only
Measurements should be taken after 5 minutes seated indoors
Avoid face washing or wiping for 10 minutes prior to measurement
Use median of two readings per point if possible

general_treatment_rules.rule: Every facial treatment must finish (last step of treatment) with Serum + Moisturizer + Sunscreen.
Add a face massage and lymphatic drainage massage wherever possible.

There is NO fixed or recommended sequence for treatment steps. The LLM is free to design ANY sequence or use DIFFERENT treatments for different facial zones based on scoring, diagnosis, and clinical logic.
